test_title: PYST 60: SSC GD Constable - Reasoning (Held On - 24 Feb, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: reasoning
question:
Three Statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statement I : **All curtains are beds.

**Statement II : **Some beds are chairs.

**Statement III : **Some chairs are not tables.

**Conclusion I :** Some chairs are tables.

**Conclusion II :** Some chairs being curtains is possible.

options.text: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow

solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ab7a5612caa255f036223256ff4e6a45e2b83f82856c8605b92dd5806132fe7.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some chairs are tables → Does not follow (As some chairs are not tables. As some part of the chairs cannot be tables, so the left part can be tables but cannot be proved, therefore it is false.)

II. Some chairs being curtains is possible → **F**ollow (As all curtains are beds and some beds are chairs. As whole curtains comes in beds which has some part common with chairs, therefore some chairs can be curtains is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion II follows.​

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3"
